To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the effect of architecture in state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods is obscured by auxiliary factors, and (b) a simple projection-based baseline performs on par or better than recent state-of-the-art approaches on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

1) recent progress in point cloud classification can largely be attributed to auxiliary factors and not the model architectures; 2) a very simple baseline, SimpleView, performs competitively or better than state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods.

(i) the auxiliary factors we mentioned above are critical to the success of point cloud classification methods; (ii) a simple projection-based method performs surprisingly well; (iii) PointNet++ performs competitively with the most recent state-of-the-art approaches, when the auxiliary factors are controlled for; and (iv) PointNet++, a network that is relatively old and small in size, performs competitively.
